chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad from Sama'ah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time for the night prayer during travel, so he said: 'From the time you pray Al-Atamah until the dawn breaks.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific time range for the night prayer during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the time for Salat al-Layl during travel extends from the performance of Al-Atamah (the late night prayer) until the emergence of true dawn (Fajr al-Sadiq). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing travelers to consolidate or delay night prayers within this extended window without the strict constraints applied to those at home.
